thread:
maya: Quick follow-up on the RFC about soft admit at the edge. Thinking we return an immediate admit token (202 + token) so the client can start streaming the body while the gateway does cheap validation + routing. Questions: 1) how do we handle client-side retries when only partial frames were sent? 2) should the admit token be single-use or allow reconnects? 3) what's the billing contract while admitted but not routed?

jon: I like the approach. My gut: token == session_id (UUID). Make it single-use for binding to a backend slot, but allow short reconnects (grace window) that reuse the token to reattach. Server keeps a tiny "inflight descriptor" (20-64 bytes) and a short durable log checkpoint for resume. Risks: memory growth and attack surface if we accept indefinite reconnects.

sana: Re billing: only count as billable when the token is forwarded to the fulfillment cluster (i.e., backend accepted it). Until then mark as "pending" and meter at a cheaper rate. Also enforce per-customer pending caps so flaky clients don't rack up cost.

frank: On retries/hedging: if the client intentionally hedges (sends multiple parallel streams), the gateway needs to enforce idempotency. For non-idempotent routes we should either reject concurrent attaches (409) or require an explicit "replay-safe" header. For partial-frame retries, attach an "offset" trailer so upstream can dedupe/apply delta.

maya: Offset trailer seems useful. Implementation note: we can use HTTP/2 trailers or gRPC trailing metadata, but mobile clients sometimes don't send trailers reliably. Alternate: periodic inline checkpoints as small JSON envelopes: {"seq":N, "ack":M} that are cheap to emit.

sana: :thinking_face: Checkpointing widens the protocol. Could we instead piggyback meta on chunk boundaries (e.g., a tiny meta chunk every ~64KB)? Also need to pick sensible TTL for pending tokens.

jon: TTL: default 30s, customer-configurable. Reattach grace window: 5s default. Memory cap: region-level cap of 10k pending descriptors; when exceeded gateway returns 503 + Retry-After and increments a metric to surface throttling.

frank: Observability bits we need: admitted.pending_count, admitted.attach_success, attach_reject_reason, attach_evictions, resume_latency_ms. Trace spans must carry session_id and attach_attempt_id. Also emit an eviction log entry with reason so SRE can correlate attacks vs normal churn.

maya: Edge cases: long-lived idle streams that are admitted but paused (client gone). Proposal: allow "soft-idle" up to 2m, then tombstone the descriptor; reattach after tombstone requires client replay or fallback. Private deployments can raise limits.

deploy-bot: canary-gateway/blue -> canary failed: ingress soft-admit test flaky in eu-west-1, requeueing job 6782

sana: I'll draft a short appendix for the protocol doc with concrete HTTP examples and a small YAML policy snippet. Putting the config we discussed here so we don't forget:

```yaml
admit_policy:
  ttl_seconds: 30
  max_pending: 10000
  allow_reattach: true
  grace_window_seconds: 5
  soft_idle_seconds: 120
  hedging_policy:
    allow_parallel: false
    reject_status: 409
```

maya: Thanks @sana @jon @frank — I'll fold these into the follow-up RFC and prototype next week unless there are objections. :thumbsup:
